1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5.name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Variation
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5.background: Possibly the oldest defence to the Ruy Lopez, played occasionally by Boris Spassky and Boris Gulko.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3.strategy: Prepares d4, which would hit the bishop with tempo, and covers d4, so Black can no longer count on ...Qd4 to defend e5. Bxc6 and Nxe5 become a real threat, which makes this the most critical answer to the early bishop.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3.name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Variation, Central Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.O-O.strategy: Castles first and prepares to defend e4 with the rook, but the king goes onto the diagonal of Black's bishop, so the f2 pawn is pinned and the rook may be tied to f1. Calm, positional play with a small edge for White rather than a sharp central fight.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.b4.strategy: Sacrifices the b-pawn to pull Black's bishop off its diagonal and then gain time with c3 and a pawn centre. Black can take the pawn and retreat with the extra material, and White must prove that the centre and open lines pay for it.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.b4.name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Variation, Spanish Wing Gambit

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3 Bb6.strategy: Steps back before d4 can hit it, keeping the bishop on the diagonal towards f2 and out of reach of the pawns. White gets to build its broad centre, so Black has to undermine it with piece play.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3 Bb6.name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Variation, Charousek Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3 Qe7.strategy: Defends e5 a second time and prepares to meet d4 with a retreat of the bishop to b6. Playable, but it brings the queen out early, blocks the e7 square, and leaves White free to build the full pawn centre it came for.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3 Qe7.name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defence, Boden Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3 f5.strategy: Counterattacks e4 at once, a sharp pawn offer that weakens the king. The better way to meet it is to strike in the centre with d4, while the weakened e8-h5 diagonal soon invites a queen check.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3 f5.name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Variation, Cordel Gambit

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3 d5.strategy: Strikes at e4 with the d-pawn, but that opens the diagonal e8-b5 and leaves the c6 knight pinned against the king. White can take on d5 or win time with Nxe5 against the pinned knight, so Black's centre play comes at the cost of tied-up pieces and a risky king.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.c3 d5.name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Variation, Konikowski Gambit

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.O-O Nd4.strategy: Hits the Spanish bishop and challenges the knight on f3 that attacks e5. If White trades, Black can recapture with the bishop and keep a sound pawn structure, but White then gains time with c3 and builds a pawn centre while the bishop retreats. A positional line with slight pressure for White.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.O-O Nd4 5..name: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defence, Zaitsev Variation
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Bc5 4.O-O Nd4 5..strategy: A gambit that offers the b-pawn to pull the bishop away from c5, the square from which it guards the knight on d4. Black can simply take the pawn, so White has to prove the activity is worth it; the quiet exchange on d4 asks far less of White.
